leftEvidence.role: The event named in public proclamation
leftEvidence.title: Killed on a tree; raised and exalted

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Before the council, Peter and the apostles answer the charge of teaching by naming obedience to God, Jesus killed on a tree, raised, exalted, and witnessed by them and the Holy Spirit.
points.right: Peter speaks in Cornelius’s house about Jesus’ ministry, death on a tree, raising, appearances to chosen witnesses, command to preach, and prophetic testimony.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.

payload.posture: Peter’s council answer and household speech both name death on a tree, divine action, and witness in different settings.

rightEvidence.role: The event named in public proclamation
rightEvidence.title: Public deeds, death on a tree, appearance, and commanded witness

payload.tension: The council scene emphasizes obedience under prohibition; the household speech emphasizes public deeds, chosen witnesses, and commanded proclamation.
payload.title: Council witness / household witness
